title: Learnability of decision tree size classes
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, and suppose a binary decision tree with real outputs computes its real-valued sign representation and has at most $s$ leaves. For any learning accuracy $\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$, run the specified Kushilevitz–Mansour learner with parameter $\varepsilon$ and size bound $\max\{1,\lceil 4s^2/\varepsilon\rceil\}$. The probability that its sign-valued hypothesis disagrees with $f$ on more than an $\varepsilon$ fraction of the sign cube is at most $1/10$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is sign-valued on the sign cube
A real-valued binary decision tree computes the real-valued sign representation of $f$
The tree has at most $s$ leaves
caveat: The formal statement specifies the learner through a large collection of definitions not described informally in the payload; the prose identifies it by its stated procedure name and parameter.
